question:
What general practices should developers follow when writing code so that attackers cannot exploit it?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Developers should follow secure coding practices spanning input validation, privilege management, error handling, dependency management, and quality assurance to prevent attackers from exploiting software vulnerabilities.

# Guidelines

- Validate all input to prevent malicious data from entering the system. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Top 10 Software Security Practices.md)
- Heed compiler warnings and keep designs simple, applying default deny principles. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Best Practices and Design Principles.md)
- Adhere to the principle of least privilege and sanitize data sent to other software. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Best Practices for Software Development.md)
- Practice defense in depth and use effective quality assurance techniques. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Security Development and Testing Practices/Software Security Best Practices.md)
- Structure code so that sections requiring extra privileges are isolated modules, as small as possible. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Software Construction Security and Privilege Management.md)
- Validate all program assumptions; if not possible, document them so maintainers know what attackers may try to invalidate. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Ensure [SWEBOK excerpt 08ff146473463cf47916] other programs. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Check every function's error status and restore prior state before terminating on security-relevant errors. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Prevent code-level security breaches such as buffer overflows or array index bounds violations. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Software Coding and Construction Testing Practices.md)
- Use defensive programming to protect routines from invalid inputs, including assertions to check input values. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Contract Design and Error Handling Strategies/Design by Contract and Defensive Programming.md)
- Use automated static code analysis tools to identify security weaknesses and common vulnerabilities. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Construction Quality Techniques and Practices.md)
- Refer to vulnerability databases (CVE, CWE, CAPEC) and use sound coding practices to reduce security defects. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Security Development and Testing Practices/Security Testing and Vulnerability Detection/Vulnerability Detection and Analysis Tools/Vulnerability Management and Security Tools.md)
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies and prevent introduction of untrusted external dependencies to reduce supply chain risk. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Methods and Languages/Dependency Management and Construction Practices/Managing Software Dependencies and Supply Chain Risks.md)
- Choose programming languages carefully, as unsafe use of languages like C/C++ increases the likelihood of security vulnerabilities. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Methods and Languages/Programming Language Notation and Security Implications/Programming Language Notations and Security Considerations.md)
- Design exception-handling policies carefully, including all relevant information in exception messages and avoiding empty catch blocks. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Contract Design and Error Handling Strategies/Error Handling, Exception Handling, and Fault Tolerance.md)
